items.title: Discord Messages in Discoverable Servers Will Soon Be Searchable on Google
items.description: Over the last decade, Discord has become the de facto community space for gaming, and there are a lot of huge servers out there that you can find by scrolling through its public servers page. But starting on November 16, some messages in these huge servers will be viewable from Google.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
Over the last decade, Discord has become the de facto community space for gaming, and there are a lot of huge servers out there that you can find by scrolling through its public servers page. But starting on November 16, some messages in these huge servers will be viewable from Google.

In a blog post, Discord laid out its plans to publish 'Server Web Pages' for every discoverable server on Discord by default. These are bespoke web pages that give a preview of a server's contents before forcing users to hit the join button. There are already several of these pages live, typically for huge online games like Rust or Dead by Daylight. These pages will be discoverable on Google, and will display a summary of the discussions going on in the server.

But while these 'Server Web Pages' will be going live next month, another update is coming in December, that'll allow answers to questions to appear in Google search. According to the blog post, "answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages."

It's important to note that only large discoverable servers will be affected by these changes, meaning your World of Warcraft guild or friend group probably won't be affected in any way. Discoverable server admins can opt out their servers or even individual channels by going to Server Settings, then Web Presence and choosing which channels you want to be visible. But, if you don't change anything, public channels will have the setting enabled by default.

If you're just a user in one of these huge servers, and you don't want your messages to be viewable from Google, you can also opt your own messages out. Simply go to User Settings, then Data and Privacy and disable 'Show my message content from Discoverable channels on web pages.'

Discord is introducing this feature to help people find answers to questions. If you've Googled anything in the last couple of years, you've probably noticed that a lot of search results for questions will lead you to Reddit, or another similar message board. It seems like Discord wants a slice of that pie.

According to the blog, "prior to Discord's launch, message boards were common, ranging from community-driven forums to official ones run by game studios. These message boards excelled at hosting long-form, structured conversations about helping people, theory crafting, and more. While they still exist today, many have moved into Discord servers. This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this."

There will likely be some useful information that you'll be able to find when these changes go live in December, but there are definitely some privacy concerns, as well. So, if you don't want your messages in large discoverable servers to be seen by everyone, make sure to disable the feature today, before all the changes go live. So far, these changes will be exclusive to large public servers with more than 1,000 members, and hopefully it stays that way.

items.title: Capcom Celebrates Record Sales in First Half of 2027 Fiscal Year, With Overwhelming Majority Being Digital Purchases
items.description: Capcom is celebrating its highest software unit sales for the first half of a fiscal year in the company’s 47-year history, with games like Monster Hunter World, Resident Evil 2, and RE7 Biohazard leading the fray.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
Capcom is celebrating its highest software unit sales for the first half of a fiscal year in the company’s 47-year history, with games like Monster Hunter World, Resident Evil 2, and RE7 Biohazard leading the fray.

It’s safe to say that 2026 was a hugely successful year for Capcom, and its next fiscal year is already looking just as rosy. In the 2026 calendar year, the developer launched three Game of the Year contenders in Resident Evil Requiem, the new but ambitious Pragmata, and Onimusha: Way of the Sword, all of which were met with critical acclaim.

These recent titles aren’t responsible for making up the bulk of its profits for its current fiscal year, though. Instead, older titles like Monster Hunter World (a live-service game that released in 2018), Resident Evil 2 Remake (2019), and Resident Evil 7: BioHazard (2017) took the top three spots in its top ten best-selling titles for the first half of its 2027 fiscal year.

Given their popularity and prestige, it’s not a massive surprise that these three titles continue to do gangbusters for Capcom almost a decade after their release. For example, in July, Resident Evil 2 Remake officially dethroned Resident Evil 5 as the series’ best-selling game at 19.75 million copies sold — a number that, as of Capcom’s latest public financial report, has increased by 2.06 million to sit at 20.38 million total copies sold.

Monster Hunter World takes the cake far and away, though, sitting at 30.83 million units sold at a 1.17 million increase. RE 7 takes third place at 20.38 million units, with a 2.06 million unit increase.

The total list of Capcom’s top ten best-selling games in the first half of its 2027 fiscal year is as follows:

  1. Monster Hunter World - 30.83m (+1.17m)
  2. Resident Evil 2 - 20.38m (+2.06m)
  3. Resident Evil 7 - 18.87m (+1.47m)
  4. Resident Evil 4 Remake - 17.5m (+3.54m)
  5. Resident Evil Village - 16.27m (+1.33m)
  6. Resident Evil 3 - 14.93m (+1.56m)
  7. Devil May Cry 5 - 14.78m (+1.83m)
  8. Resident Evil Requiem - 8.51m (+1.59m)
  9. Pragmata - 2.73m
  10. Onimusha: Way of the Sword - 1.78m

It's worth noting that the newest Monster Hunter entry, Monster Hunter Wilds, isn't listed on here. However, the previous game in the series is still a juggernaut for Capcom, going to show just how unpopular Wilds is following oodles of player complaints in the year since it's February 2025 launch... and that's even after Capcom 'permanently' slashed the game's price.

According to Capcom's financial report, these figures mark the company's highest-ever total and catalog unit sales for an H1 period, and most of them were digital. This same report shows that a staggering 92.4% of sales were digital, with 57.1% coming from PC and 35.3% from consoles. In stark comparison, physical units make up just 7.6% of sales. (This is actually a bit of a drop from its previously reported digital sales figures back in Q1 2026, which was listed at 93.3%.)

This all comes hot off the heels of Capcom’s two newest film adaptations, with Zach Cregger’s Resident Evil movie becoming the most profitable in the series’ history and Street Fighter launching to number one at the box office during its opening weekend (news of a sequel, however, is still up in the air).

Pragmata also performed well for Capcom, with corporate officer Yoshikazu Shimauchi suggesting that sales were so good that the likelihood of a sequel is high. Combine that with Onimusha selling one million copies on day one, it’s clear that 2026 is Capcom’s year. Now, we just need to see how The Game Awards pan out.

items.title: 'Physical Books, But Not Physical Games?' — PlayStation Book Announcement Prompts Confusion Over Sony's Physical Media Stance
items.description: Preorders have opened for PlayStation: The First 30 Years, a physical book honoring the gaming giant’s tenured history, but fans aren't exactly in a celebratory mood.
items.author: Blythe Dujardin
items.content:
Preorders have opened for PlayStation: The First 30 Years, a physical book honoring the gaming giant’s tenured history, but fans aren't exactly in a celebratory mood. The book’s announcement comes as Sony faces continued criticism for its decision to cut disc production, prompting confusion over the new physical media release and an influx of “No Disc, No Buy” replies.

The book itself is a collaboration between PlayStation and Read-Only Memory, a UK-based publisher focused on “premium” gaming and world-building books. A widely available Standard edition is listed at $125, while a Deluxe Edition, listed at $325, will only be available in 1994 copies. Both editions are now up for preorder exclusively from Read-Only Memory, shipping this November.

According to the official listing, the 400-page book “is the definitive visual chronicle of Sony’s world-changing videogame console, marking its 30th anniversary with unprecedented access to the company’s archive of R&D prototypes, concept sketches, and development models.” It collects “insights from the engineers and designers who shaped PlayStation’s identity,” including the “Father of PlayStation,” Ken Kutaragi, the original DualShock designer, Teiyu Goto, and the chief designer on the PS5, Yujin Morisawa.

Sneak peek images show early designs of DualShock controllers and PlayStation consoles — complete with beautiful disc drives.

Fans were quick to point out the curious decision to celebrate the gaming brand’s history with a physical media release. “Just selling collectibles and taking away what we actually want to collect,” said one X user with a sequence of disc emojis. “Just so we’re clear… You support physical books, but not physical games?” replied another.

Earlier this year, Sony announced that it would be cutting disc production for PlayStation consoles starting in 2028. Despite immediate backlash, Sony has stood by the decision. But gamers refuse to back down, taking over the comment sections on pretty much anything PlayStation-related.

While the online backlash is louid, it remains to be seen whether it will affect future launches of physical collectibles, digital games, or even the PS6. Ken Kutaragi, who is featured in the new book, recently backed the studio’s decision, acknowledging that “physical discs have become a metaphor for ‘owning’ games” but ultimately seeing the decision to cut production as “economically reasonable.”

While PlayStation has seen a continued decline in physical disc sales, critics argue that “ownership” is an essential part of gaming communities. Building up your physical game collection has long been a source of pride for any PlayStation, Xbox, or Nintendo fan, while also allowing for sharing and re-selling.

Former PlayStation boss Shawn Layden has been one voice speaking out against the business decision, saying, “If you can't sell a thing, it means you don't own a thing. If you don't own it, then what are you buying?” As PlayStation continues to look back on its 30-year-history, it’s clear that this decision will define its future.

items.title: World of Warcraft Forever Name Reservation Is Broken Ahead of Launch
items.description: The World of Warcraft Forever beta ended last week, and in the space in between that and the full launch on November 4, Blizzard is offering players the ability to reserve character names ahead of launch. There's only one problem, the system looks like it's broken.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
The World of Warcraft Forever beta ended last week, and in the space in between that and its full launch on November 4, Blizzard is offering players the ability to reserve character names ahead of release. There's only one problem: the system looks like it's broken.

Right now, the name reservation system is only supposed to be available in Europe, with North American servers getting a name reservation window starting at 1pm PT/4pm ET today. But the WoW Forever team has issued a message to players in the Battle.net client, saying "World of Warcraft: Forever Name Reservations are delayed while we resolve some final technical issues. Thank you for your patience!"

The way the name reservation system is supposed to work is that, by launching the latest version of WoW Forever, players will be able to pick a ruleset (PvE, PvP, etc,) and then create up to three characters with reserved names. But, for a lot of European players, the blue 'Play' button on the Battle.net launcher is grayed out, meaning they can't even get into the game to try and make a new character.

Just like with any sort of World of Warcraft delay, players have taken to the WoW forums to voice their discontent, in a massive 120-post thread. Player Equinox posted, "There is literally nothing going right the first time something new launches. It's ridiculous how they manage it every time to screw things up." Meanwhile, Katerlina asked, "They did this already for USA right? Or are we the test?" And, no, Blizzard has not launched the feature in the U.S. quite yet.

Some players have found a workaround that gets them in the game, but it doesn't seem to be doing a lot of good right now. Aureliani posted "Go to install folder of forever and just start wow.exe, use email + password, and that at least brings me to the rulesets (that are still greyed out though)."

While it probably won't get you into the game any faster, player Bìsh has some helpful advice, saying, "If the PLAY button its greyed out, that means your launcher was set in another region. I dunno why, but mine was set to Americas. I logged out from Battlenet, I clicked switch accounts to clear the name of the account also, and in the right corner there is a cog where you can put it back to Europe. After I've done that, the PLAY button its not greyed out anymore."

There are only a couple more hours before this feature launches in the U.S., and unless Blizzard figures out the root cause of this issue ahead of time, it's likely that NA players are going to experience delays, too. Either way, hopefully these kinds of issues aren't present when WoW Forever gets its full launch on November 4.

Ahead of WoW Forever's launch, we got a chance to sit down with Blizzard principal game designer Kris Zierhut to talk about the future of the MMO. It sounds like updates will be coming regularly, and we might get a chance to visit some of the continents that got added in expansions, like Northrend and Pandaria.

items.title: Best Buy’s Black Friday Sale Schedule Announced
items.description: Best Buy has taken to its corporate blog to announce the retailer's full holiday sale schedule, including Black Friday and last-minute Christmas sales.
items.author: Chris Reed
items.content:
Retailers have begun to announce their Black Friday sale schedules. Following hot on the heels of Walmart's announcement this morning, Best Buy has unveiled its entire holiday 2026 sale schedule — including Black Friday. It’s comprised of several sale events that run between October 30 and December 24.

Here’s the full Best Buy holiday sale schedule:

  • October 30 - November 1: DoorBOOsters
  • November 6 - November 19: Early Black Friday Deals + Doorbusters
  • November 19 - 28: Black Friday Doorbusters + Deals
  • November 29 - 30: Cyber Monday Sale Event
  • December 18 - 24: Last-Minute Savings Event

The sales kick off with the DoorBOOsters sale that runs October 30 through November 1. We don’t have details about what deals will be available at this point, but we'll be sure to cover the sales right here at IGN.

Following a brief five-day break, the official “Early Black Friday Deals + Doorbusters” sale begins on November 6. This sounds like a general sale that will run all month. However, Best Buy says “new deals will drop every Friday” during this time.

The actual Black Friday Doorbusters and Deals sale starts on November 19 and runs through November 28 (the day after Black Friday). These will be the real deals, though based on previous years, you can generally expect new deals to go live on Black Friday itself (November 27).

If stock holds out, Black Friday deals typically stay live throughout the weekend. Best Buy’s Cyber Monday Sale Event kicks off Sunday, November 29 and runs through Monday, November 30. These deals are not typically very different from the Black Friday deals, though some retailers get resupplies of stock on Cyber Monday. So if you missed out on any Black Friday deals, it’s worth checking back on Monday to see if it’s available again.

It’s also worth noting that, if you happen to be a Best Buy Plus or Total member, you’ll earn double rewards on purchases from November 19 to December 6.

After effectively an entire month of sales at Best Buy, the retailer is giving it a rest through the first two weeks of December. But starting December 18 and running through December 24 (aka Christmas Eve), you can expect to see more deals go live in what Best Buy is calling its Last-Minute Savings sale.

If you buy something from Best Buy between October 30 - December 31 and want to return it, you have until January 15 to make the return for most items. You can find more details about what to expect from the sale in Best Buy’s corporate blog post.

items.title: GTA 6 Sparks Unlikely Cliff Richard Resurgence, but the 86-Year-Old Singer Still Doesn't Know What It Is
items.description: British singer Cliff Richard is enjoying an unlikely resurgence at the age of 86 after one of his old songs featured in the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix, but it seems the whole Rockstar Games phenomenon has passed him by.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
British singer Cliff Richard is enjoying an unlikely resurgence at the age of 86 after one of his old songs featured in the GTA 6 Extended Look on Netflix, but it seems the whole Rockstar Games phenomenon has passed him by.

"Devil Woman" is a 1976 single from his album I'm Nearly Famous, and it previously got a bump in popularity after featuring on 2017 movie I, Tonya. But nothing compares GTA 6, a game widely expected to be the biggest entertainment launch in history.

Since the Extended Look, Devil Woman has seen a 325% increase in daily streams. The singer himself doesn’t really understand what’s happening here.

In an interview with The Times, Richard admitted he didn't know what Grand Theft Auto was, despite Rockstar paying out to feature it on the extensive GTA 6 soundtrack.

“I was told this happened!” he said. “My nephew, who has two boys, said they came screaming to him, ‘Dad, it’s Uncle Cliff!’ They didn’t realise I could sing like that. The show is a game show, isn’t it, really? One of the biggest on TV?”

He got the word “game” right, so let’s give him that. The man is 86, after all. Even if he doesn’t fully understand the extent of what’s going on, however, he’s happy that his music is still relevant in the big 2026.

“People will no longer just say, ‘Oh, Cliff Richard is from the past,’” he said. “Because I am, but that past is what makes everything what it is today.”

Rockstar recently revealed some of the musical tracks you’ll hear while cruising around Vice City, in its GTA 6 radio stations and song list. As well as the oldies, there will be tracks from contemporary music legends such as Yung Lean and Travis Scott.

GTA 6 is scheduled for launch on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series consoles.

Photo by Karwai Tang/WireImage.

items.title: 'A Lot of Players Don't Want to Play a Monster' – WoW Forever Principal Designer Sheds More Light on Why the Skyborne Were Added
items.description: World of Warcraft Forever has its full launch a week from now on November 4, but ahead of time, Blizzard principal game designer Kris Zierhut shared a little bit of insight on why the new Skyborne race was added to the game.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
World of Warcraft Forever has its full launch a week from now on November 4, but ahead of time, Blizzard principal game designer Kris Zierhut shared a little bit of insight on why the new Skyborne race was added to the game.

When I asked Zierhut about Skyborne's addition, he told me that the goal was to add more elves to the game but to maintain the faction balance in the process. "We knew that we wanted to bring in more of the elves into the game. We know they're the most popular races in World of Warcraft historically. And in particular, the current alliance and Horde races from the Classic Era have the unfortunate feature that they tend to cause a faction imbalance," he told me.

As for why Blizzard needed to add elves specifically, it's because there's a segment of the player base that doesn't want to play some of WoW's more unique races. Zierhut explained, "There's a certain... a lot of players who don't want to play a monster, to put it really honestly. They don't want to be an Orc or a Troll or a Tauren or Undead. They want to have something that looks prettier. It's not everybody."

There are other possibilities for elves in Azeroth, like the Blood Elves, but the Forever team doesn't want to step on the retail team's toes. Elsewhere in the interview, I asked about Silvermoon, the home of the Blood Elves, and Zierhut referenced that, saying, "You mentioned Silvermoon, and this is a story that Retail had recently told, and we didn't want to get in each other's way of telling that story. We want to give them time to let their Silvermoon story breathe and do everything they wanted with it. And then once they were done with it, we could maybe then go visit Silvermoon."

So, it sounds like there's a chance that the Blood Elves could come to the game in the future, but for now, players will just have to make do with the Skyborne if they want a Horde elf race.

Ahead of Forever coming out next week, Blizzard has also detailed how often players can expect new updates, which will be added slower than the quick eight-week patch cycle of the modern game. Zierhut has also told me that the Forever team is looking at visiting some of the locations we've been to in expansions, like Northrend and Pandaria, in future updates.

items.title: Blizzard Reveals Plan for World of Warcraft Forever Update Frequency
items.description: World of Warcraft Forever launches a week from today, and while the game will have a huge swath of content available on day one, there will be new content continually added to the game. But how frequently should fans expect new content to arrive? It sounds like Blizzard is willing to take things a little slower than in the modern version of World of Warcraft.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
World of Warcraft Forever launches a week from today, and while the game will have a huge swath of content available on day one, there will be new content continually added to the game. But how frequently should fans expect new content to arrive? It sounds like Blizzard is willing to take things a little slower than in the modern version of World of Warcraft.

In a recent interview with IGN, World of Warcraft Forever principal game designer Kris Zierhut, said Forever will employ a slower cadence than Midnight's aggressive eight-week content cycle: "We're fairly convinced the correct [update] rate is something closer to once every four months or 17 weeks or three times a year."

This is in contrast with the modern version of World of Warcraft, which has had an aggressive update cadence since Dragonflight launched in 2022. And while that approach has meant players of the modern version of the game have something new every couple of months, some have said the updates often feels rushed, with bugs and repeated content. We've all done some form of invasions several times in the last couple of years, after all.

Zierhut did say that Blizzard experimented with a faster update schedule in Season of Discovery, an experimental Classic game mode that came out in 2023, but "we cut it down to closer to that eight week or 10 week schedule. It felt way, way, way too fast."

But by going with a four month update schedule, Forever will also avoid the content droughts that some older expansions were infamous for. There have been times in WoW's history where the game didn't have new content for a year at a time, like in Warlords of Draenor, where patch 6.2, which included Hellfire Citadel, lasted for 13 months before the prepatch update for Legion.

Zierhut acknowledged this as well, saying: "We've played around with different rates of releasing content and going six or eight months without new stuff always feels bad. We know that."

Just because World of Warcraft patches will be released in four-month intervals, it doesn't necessarily mean you'll have to wait four months for something new to do. Zierhut also told me that the team may timegate some content, saying "one nuance on that is we do plan on making content that unlocks in between. So you might have patches with major releases four months apart, but there may be things that unlock two or three months in or one month into that."

The idea there is to ease players into content, rather than overwhelming them with everything all at once. Zierhut continued: "It's not just patch day comes [around], here's a content fire hose, and now we're silent for four months. A lot of that is, 'hey, there's a time event calendar that gradually unlocks things and opens them up over those four months' to give things a little bit more life instead of that all at once effect."

Only time will tell if this middle ground between rapid updates and slow updates will pay off, but according to the roadmap that Blizzard released at BlizzCon, Forever will have its first major update sometime in spring 2027. So, if that four-month timeline that Blizzard is targeting pays off, WoW Forever should have a fresh round of new content sometime in March.

While you wait for the game to launch, check out more on Blizzard's plan for World of Warcraft Forever.

items.title: Blizzard Teases Familiar Locations for Post-Launch World of Warcraft Forever Updates
items.description: World of Warcraft Forever gets its full release on November 4, and while the MMO will stay tethered to the two vanilla continents, Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, it sounds like future updates could add some of the areas we've visited in the expansions.
items.author: Jacqueline Thomas
items.content:
World of Warcraft Forever gets its full release on November 4, and while the MMO will stay tethered to the two vanilla continents, Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, it sounds like future updates could add some of the areas we've visited in the expansions.

I recently got a chance to sit down with Blizzard principal game designer Kris Zierhut to talk about the future of WoW Forever, and when I asked him if there were threads the developer could pull at to find new content "without going to outer space," Zierhut responded by saying: "Correct, correct. Now, that said, the Dark Portal exists, Northrend exists, Pandaria exists, and we could make minor forays into those areas. We might have a dungeon or a quest that takes you there for a mission or two and come back."

So, rather than going to these places for these multi-year epic quests, like going to Northrend to stop Arthas, it seems like these would be little jaunts to a different part of the world, then quickly returning back to the vanilla continents.

Zierhut emphasized that any journeys to other parts of Azeroth would be brief, saying: "But the key detail there is Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor are your home. You don't have capital cities, you don't have auction houses and innkeepers and things like that outside of Eastern Kingdom and Kalimdor. We won't introduce new capital cities in this plan. Okay. You always come home."

Later on in the interview, Zierhut clarified that the versions of these continents wouldn't be the same as what we've visited in the expansions. Using Northrend as an example, he told me: "If we ever went to Northrend, we wouldn't be visiting the version that you see in Wrath of the Lich King. But could we visit some extremely hostile level 60 version of it because Arthas is still in the stage where he's sending Kel’Thuzad to Eastern Kingdoms to assault Eastern Plaguelands? We could. There's so much that we can do with the timeline that we're in."

While it seems like working in areas from the expansions would run counter to Forever's mission statement, the developers are more focused on maintaining the spirit of classic WoW, rather than strictly adhering to the same content that we played in 2004 and 2019. For instance, Blizzard took a pretty early stance against adding features like group tagging, because it wanted players to group up and do content together. But, later on, it added the 'Kyle's Gone Missing' quest, even though it intially came out as a part of The Burning Crusade, because it fit with the spirit of the original game.

Forever is also adding entirely new parts of the world, including some maps, like Mount Hyjal, that were originally supposed to be part of the original World of Warcraft, but didn't make the final cut. It's going to be interesting to see what direction future content is going to go in, because unlike other versions of Classic, Blizzard doesn't have to rigidly stick to what World of Warcraft did in the past. One thing's for sure, though, we won't have to wait as long between patches as some of the older WoW expansions.

items.title: South Korean Politician Urges President to Play Modern Warfare 4 to Understand 'Devastation' of Potential Invasion
items.description: A South Korean politician has urged the country's President to play Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 to grasp the potential devastation from a North Korean invasion.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
A South Korean politician has urged the country's President to play Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 to grasp the potential devastation of a North Korean invasion.

In a report from Korean outlet The Herald Business, politician Han Dong-hoon urged President Lee Jae-myung to play Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 to grasp how catastrophic things could be if the country was ill-equipped to defend against a North Korean invasion. He noted that the country should be actively preparing for any kind of situation, rather than simply hoping it never happens. He also pushed back against critiques of the game depicting an active all-out war between the two countries, believing that it should be a wake-up call to assess whether or not they're prepared for something like that to happen.

"I hope the image of a Seoul reduced to ashes in the game remains in the realm of fiction," he said.

In Modern Warfare 4, the game opens with a group of South Korean soldiers patrolling the city streets before an EMP takes out all power in the area. The North Korean army then attacks the city with a barrage of missiles before air-dropping soldiers and launching offensive measures through a series of tunnels. It's pure chaos, not unlike the surprise Russian invasion of America in the original Modern Warfare 2 from 2009.

Half of Modern Warfare 4's story focuses on South Korean forces trying to push the North Korean opposition back, despite being hopelessly outmatched and overpowered, partially thanks to a groundbreaking new technology that can wipe out defenses in the blink of an eye. The story also feels oddly timed, as reports last week claimed that North Korean leader Kim Jong Un had fallen into a coma or even outright died.

These reports have been denied and countered, but the comparison to the game came as Kim Jong Un's sister, Kim Yo Jong, made threats against South Korea. In Modern Warfare 4, there's a familial power struggle within North Korean leadership, which ends with the Supreme Leader's sister taking command and unleashing war on South Korea. Given the timing of the real-life situation and the release of Modern Warfare 4 last week, it was hard for fans not to see eerie similarities between reality and the game's fictional story.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 also has an entire mode set in the DMZ, a real-world location that sits on the border of North and South Korea. In the game, the player explores this environment to complete missions, extract loot, and learn additional lore about the game's story. IGN gave Modern Warfare 4 a 7/10, noting that the game's multiplayer feels a bit too familiar, but the campaign elevates the larger package: "Multiplayer may not quite hit the mark, but a great campaign ensures Modern Warfare 4's place as one of Call of Duty’s better recent entries," reads an excerpt from our review.

items.title: Matthew Lillard Calls His Superman 2 Character 'A Very James Gunn Moment'
items.description: Superman 2: Man of Tomorrow brings Daredevil: Born Again actor Matthew Lillard into the wider James Gunn DCU, but comic fans might not recognize his character.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Superman 2: Man of Tomorrow brings Daredevil: Born Again actor Matthew Lillard into the wider James Gunn DCU, but comic fans might not recognize his character. Man of Tomorrow mixes a returning cast with fresh characters as David Corenswelt’s Superman agrees to an unsteady alliance with Nicholas Hoult's Lex Luthor.

Brainiac is the antagonist this time, giving us a bigger-brained baddie than Superman’s bald-headed human rival. A guy with a bigger brain is basically Luthor’s own kryptonite.

Rachel Brosnahan will return as Lois Lane and Skyler Gisondo is back as Jimmy Olsen. These returning cast members will bump into players from the wider DCU, including Blue Beetle and the Justice Gang. Matthew Lillard’s role in all this, however, has not been announced.

On a promotional tour for Prime Video’s adaptation of Carrie, Lillard was asked whether his character is someone comic fans will recognise or not. Fan theories that he would play the DCU’s Barry Allen were previously shot down by DC Studios co-CEO James Gunn.

"It's a very James Gunn moment,” Lillard told The Direct. “So, I wouldn't worry too much about finding him in the comics."

While short and sweet, it does suggest Lillard will play an original character, rather than someone already established in the comics. Gunn has already introduced a range of original characters to the DCU, including Amanda Waller's daughter and Mister Handsome.

Here’s everything we know about the plot of Superman 2: Man of Tomorrow so far. Fans are also speculating about who Gunn will cast as Wonder Woman — probably not Lillard.

Gunn recently shot down rumors that Milly Alcock had been fired from her role as Supergirl. "Oh brother," his post said at the time. "You guys just have to stop listening to BS, and I'm mostly done shooting down rumors, as there are so many and I'm not on here much."

Man of Tomorrow is scheduled to be released in theaters on July 9, 2027.

items.title: Kingdom Come: Deliverance Developer Hit by 'Serious' Cybersecurity Incident
items.description: Warhorse Studios — the developer behind Kingdom Come: Deliverance, its sequel and an upcoming Lord of the Rings RPG — has been hit by a “serious” cyberattack.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Warhorse Studios — the developer behind Kingdom Come: Deliverance, its sequel, and an upcoming Lord of the Rings RPG — has been hit by a “serious” cyberattack. The company announced the news on its website.

The developer is currently working with cybersecurity experts to “secure its systems, investigate the incident, and assess its full impact.” Warhorse has also reached out to authorities to track down the culprits, who accessed company systems and data.

“This is a serious incident for Warhorse Studios and everyone affected,” said Martin Frývaldský, CEO of Warhorse Studios. “Our immediate priority is to secure our systems, establish the full extent of the breach, and take the necessary steps to protect our employees, partners, and community.

“We are dedicating the resources needed to address this situation and will communicate further information as soon as we responsibly can.”

Warhorse said it won’t comment further or conduct any interviews on the topic, so the extent of the attack isn’t clear at the moment. The studio will share updates as it can.

Warhorse Studios is currently working on a Lord of the Rings role-playing game, described as an “open world Middle-earth RPG,” and a new Kingdom Come game expected to be Kingdom Come: Deliverance 3 or a spinoff.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 launched last year to critical and commercial acclaim. IGN's Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 review returned a 9/10. We said: "Armed with excellent melee combat and an exceptional story, Kingdom Come: Deliverance 2 is one part sequel and one part coronation, bringing a lot of the original's ideas to fruition."

While Warhorse has enjoyed significant success with Kingdom Come: Deliverance, it has come under fire recently for its use of generatve AI. Daniel Vávra, the previous director of Kingdom Come: Deliverance, stepped down from his role in February to focus on making a Kingdom Come: Deliverance movie.

This month, Japanese developer Capcom was also hit with a cyberattack which saw 196 customer accounts compromised. Retailer Playasia was also taken offline. These hacks coincide with what security experts have dubbed “Black October” in which AI agents have disrupted internet security. It isn’t clear if Capcom, Playasai, or the Warhorse hack is related to that.

items.title: Silent Hill Remake Coming 2027, First Cast Details Leaked
items.description: The 1999 PS1 horror game is getting the Bloober treatment, and a new leak from MP1ST suggests work has been underway since 2022 and the game is targeting a 2027 launch.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
With Silent Hill 2’s remake selling 6 million copies, it’s no surprise Bloober Team and Konami would want to have another crack at things. Last year, the Polish developer and Japanese publisher confirmed they were doing just that with a remake of the first Silent Hill.

The 1999 PS1 horror game is getting the Bloober treatment, and a new leak from MP1ST suggests work has been underway since 2022 and the game is targeting a 2027 launch.

According to the report, the game cast its actors under the codename “Project Noise,” and features Gabrielle Fritz and Jade Matthew in major roles.

Fritz has worked in other games, from Battlefield 2042 to Wolfenstein 2: The New Colossus, as well as a range of TV shows. Matthew is best known for British TV appearances.

While it isn’t clear what roles the two actors play in Silent Hill’s remake, the report speculated that police officer Cybil Bennett, nurse Lisa Garland, or primary antagonist Dahlia Gillespie would fit. There’s no word on who could play protagonist Harry Mason yet.

Bloober Team is also working on DLC for Cronos: The New Dawn, its multiplayer horror game, Saw: Genesis, and story-driven adventure Star Trek: Shadow Frontier.

The 2027 release window lines up with Konami’s recent spate of Silent Hill projects, with Townfall launching this year and Silent Hill f in 2025, giving us a new Silent Hill project each year. You can check out the games in order in our Silent Hill timeline.

Konami is planning "second and third waves" of new Silent Hill games, according to producer Motoi Okamoto, who pointed at Silent Hill 2 Remake, Silent Hill f, and Silent Hill: Townfall as the first wave.

That would make a remake of the first game the beginning of the second wave of new Silent Hill projects. It’ll be interesting to see what comes after.

items.title: Pokemon Unite to Be Taken Offline in 2027, In-Game Sales Suspended Immediately
items.description: Pokemon Unite will end service on March 23, 2027, following the game’s final competition, the Aeos Crown 2027, just two days prior in Tokyo.
items.author: Kirk McKeand
items.content:
Pokemon Unite will end service on March 23, 2027, following the game’s final competition, the Aeos Crown 2027, just two days prior in Tokyo. The MOBA Pokemon battler will be shut down on both Nintendo Switch and mobile.

According to The Pokemon Company, Aeos Gem sales have been halted immediately along with any new Unite Club memberships and automatic renewals.

“We offer our sincerest gratitude to the many Trainers who have played since service started for the Nintendo Switch version on July 21, 2021,” said the announcement. “We hope you continue to enjoy Pokémon Unite until the final day of service.”

Once the game closes, players will be able to view their stats and achievements, and even play practice rounds, but online matches won’t be available. To do so, you’ll need to download a new library feature.

"Even after service ends, players who complete the required library data download before Tuesday, March 23, 2027, at 00:00 UTC will be able to use the library feature to view certain records and in-game content,” the announcement said. “Players who do not complete the required download before service ends will not be able to use the library feature afterward.”

Many expected the news after Pokemon Unite was conspicuously absent from the Pokemon World Championships 2027’s list of games. The final update lands in November, along with a special event where players can grab Unite licenses, Holowear, and other items.

Pokémon Unite was originally released on July 21, 2021, for the Nintendo Switch, and on September 22, 2021, for Android and iOS mobile devices.

IGN’s 6/10 Pokemon Unite review called it “an entertaining casual MOBA constrained by its overcommitment to simplicity (and some questionable microtransactions).” At least those are gone now.

Here’s a list of every Pokemon game you can play on Switch right now. We’ll update that when Unite ends service in 2027.

items.title: Dead by Daylight Devs Explain Chucky's Exit From Stores and Says Horror Icons Removed Due to Licenses Have 'Open Invitation' to Rejoin
items.description: Dead by Daylight developer Behaviour Interactive has responded after confirming Chucky would be removed from stores last week, explaining that horror icons will "continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin)."
items.author: Michael Cripe
items.content:
Dead by Daylight developer Behaviour Interactive has responded after confirming Chucky would be removed from stores last week, explaining that horror icons will "continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin)."

There was a bit of confusion amongst fans when the studio behind the hit asymmetrical horror game announced Chucky as the latest icon to leave its roster. Following the removal of Pinhead last year and Michael Myers just months ago, fans were sad to see another Killer exit stores so soon.

However, it's ultimately not up to Behaviour when it comes to the date some franchises may depart. In a statement sent to IGN, Behaviour said that, while its "goal is always to keep licenses" in Dead by Daylight forever, that can't always be the case. That's why, "despite our best efforts," Chucky and others have left and could continue to leave in the future.

No one wants to see Dead by Daylight's staggering roster of Killers and Survivors shrink for any reason, especially when Behaviour has consistently delivered variety in the decade since its launch. Unfortunately, that's what will happen come November 24, 2026, when the Chucky Chapter is made unavailable to purchase.

The upside, as Behaviour made clear in last week's announcement, is that anyone who purchases the possessed killer doll and any of his accompanying cosmetics will have the freedom to use them beyond the cutoff date. It means that, while Chucky may show up in fewer lobbies over time, he'll never truly be gone.

It's something Behaviour made sure to reiterate in its statement to IGN, reassuring fans that "Dead by Daylight will always be gaming's House of Horror." This means that, even when licenses expire, the Child's Play, Halloween, and Hellraiser franchises will always have the same invitation to enter the Fog that newcomers have. You can see the studio's full statement on Chucky's exit below.

"As with all live service games, players can expect regular updates, new content, and occasional changes over time," Behaviour said. "Our goal is always to keep licenses in our game forever. When they have to go away, it's because - despite our best efforts - it wasn't possible to retain them.

"We want to reassure our community that Chucky will remain part of the Dead by Daylight experience for existing owners. Players who already own The Good Guy, his perks, or any associated cosmetics will still be able to use that content after November 24, 2026.

"Dead by Daylight will always be gaming's House of Horror, and horror icons will continue to have an open invitation to join (or rejoin) us in the Fog."

It'll be painful to see one of Dead by Daylight's more unique Killers leave the Fog, but a return is definitely not off the table. One of the more famous examples of an IP leaving and eventually coming back was Stranger Things and its playable Demogorgon, which was removed from stores in November 2021 before being added back in November 2023.

For now, there's no telling when Chucky and Child's Play may return. Meanwhile, we recently found out that Terrifier's Art the Clown would enter the fray starting next month. Friday the 13th's Jason was added in June. For more, you can check out everything Behaviour announced during its 10th Anniversary Broadcast over the summer.

items.title: You Can Play Buckshot Roulette in Real Life at this Tokyo Cafe — and Even Drink an Arctic Eggs Cocktail
items.description: The Ukiyo Game Bar & Cafe in Tokyo is going viral for its unique guest experience that lets customers play Buckshot Roulette in real life… well, sort of.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
The Ukiyo Game Bar & Cafe in Tokyo is going viral for its unique guest experience that lets customers play Buckshot Roulette in real life… well, sort of.

Two or more guests can make their reservations to play a game of Buckshot Roulette, with reservations open in blocks from month to month. Of course, this isn’t actual Russian Roulette (which would be extremely dangerous, not to mention wildly illegal), but instead a fun recreation of the viral indie game with non-lethal mechanics. (For instance, if you get 'shot,' you have to take a 'shot.')

As shown in a tweet posted by the bar and photos shared by guests, hosts will don a mask of the dealer’s terrifying face and wield a prop shotgun as players gather round the roulette table with their drinks in tow. (This roulette table, first made for Tokyo Game Show, is now a permanent fixture at Ukiyo Game Bar & Cafe.)

リアルバックショットテーブル 11月9日まで予約解放！

お二人様から予約可能です。

予約は以下のフォームかDMからで！

お待ちしております。 https://t.co/ffPD4M20sb

— UKIYO GAME BAR ＆ CAFE｜プレオープン中 (@ukiyogamebar) October 21, 2026

played irl buckshot roulette at @ukiyogamebar and I cannot stress enough how much fun this was. BIG recommend for anyone visiting Tokyo! https://t.co/yowJEXRP5s

— maria (@eurothug4000) October 26, 2026

Speaking of drinks, Ukiyo Game Bar also has a few themed cocktails on offer, one of which is themed after the hit indie game Arctic Eggs. Made in collaboration with the game’s developer, The Water Museum, this delightful drink even features a gummy in the shape of a fried egg. (These gummies aren’t actually available in Japan; an American staff member shipped 2 kilos worth of them in from the States.)

Photos of the Buckshot Roulette experience quickly went viral on social media, leaving fans with severe FOMO and scrambling to make travel plans.

In Buckshot Roulette, players sign a waiver and engage in a version of Russian Roulette with a Shotgun against a mysterious and terrifying opponent. There’s more to it than pulling the trigger and hoping you don’t meet a grisly end; there are a variety of items on offer that players can use to their advantage and tip the odds in their favor with the goal of surviving — and making off with a major cash prize.

この目玉焼きのグミ日本で売ってなくてアメリカのスタッフが2キロ持ってきてくれました。

売り切れ御免なのでまだの方はぜひ！

Collaborating with @critical_reflex and @WaterMuseum_ for the Arctic “Big Egg”cocktail at the UKIYO GAME BAR.

Thanks for delivering the eggs @dbloodworth2

— UKIYO GAME BAR ＆ CAFE｜プレオープン中 (@ukiyogamebar) October 9, 2026

Buckshot Roulette also boasts a multiplayer mode if you’d like to raise the stakes with your friends. The game is published by Critical Reflex, home to a bunch of other quirky, viral indie games like Mouthwashing, No, I’m not a Human, and even Arctic Eggs. All three of those games are now available to play on Xbox, as revealed during the 2026 ID@Xbox showcase this month.

Image Credits: Ukiyo Game Bar, Twitter/X

items.title: DC Studios Boss Confirms Discussions With Alan Ritchson, but Haven't Found a Role for Him Yet
items.description: DC Studios boss Peter Safran confirms they've had conversations with Alan Ritchson for a variety of roles, but are still looking to find the right one.
items.author: Cade Onder
items.content:
DC Studios boss Peter Safran confirms they've had conversations with Alan Ritchson for a variety of roles, but are still looking to find the right one.

When speaking with Collider, Safran confirmed that Ritchson is an actor with whom DC Studios has had several conversations and wants to utilize. He noted that they've eyed him for a handful of projects, but none of them have come to fruition.

Although the actor has been heavily speculated about and is on fans' wishlist to play the DCU's Batman, it doesn't sound like that's the role DC wants him for. However, DC sees more in him than just a big badass brawler, which is the kind of role he's best known for (see: Reacher).

"[...] He's just good," said Safran. "I also think there's a lot more depth to him than you might have seen. I think there's more that he can do that people haven't seen."

It's unclear what roles he could play. Obviously, given his size, he's a great fit for someone like Bane, Deathstroke, or some other physically imposing character. However, it sounds like Safran is trying to find something that allows him to flex his acting chops and show off his range. DC is currently producing a film centered around Bane and Deathstroke, so it's possible he ends up playing one of those characters, but it's hard to say right now.

Although Robert Pattinson is currently firmly seated in the role of Batman, he's not expected to play the character in the DCU. Pattinson himself has even noted that the tonal difference between his DC universe and James Gunn's might be too jarring. Instead, the DCU is expected to introduce an older Batman with a son, Damian Wayne. It's unclear when we will actually see him or when we will learn who is playing him, as the project was announced nearly four years ago and has received very few updates.

The DCU's Batman was briefly seen in Creature Commandos, but it wasn't anything super notable. The character does not appear in DC's Clayface movie, either, so the studio is clearly trying to find the right way to properly introduce him. Maybe he'll be in next year's Man of Tomorrow, but we'll just have to wait and see.

items.title: Canceled Transformers Game Footage Leaks Online, Showing Never-Before-Seen Final Trailer
items.description: A final trailer for the canceled game Transformers: Reactivate has leaked online, giving fans the closest look at what the completed project might’ve looked like.
items.author: Virginia Glaze
items.content:
A final trailer for the canceled game, Transformers: Reactivate, has leaked online, giving fans the closest look at what the completed project might’ve looked like.

Transformers: Reactivate, a third-person online action game made by developer Splash Damage, was first revealed at the 2022 Game Awards. The title faced major delays after its big reveal and was eventually canned in January 2025, with Splash Damage undergoing several rounds of layoffs in the nearly two years since then.

Just a day after the project was put to bed, gameplay footage from the highly-anticipated title leaked online, showing Bumblebee blasting enemies and traversing terrain in his vehicle form.

It’s been more than a year since this footage found its way on social media, but in a miraculous turn of events, one fan has managed to uncover a final trailer for the game with what seems to be the most complete build we’ve seen thus far.

The trailer was uploaded to X/Twitter on October 26, 2026 by a user named 'Nem - TFR Archives' who, by their own admission, preserves Transformers: Reactive content because they "need to cope somehow."

Preceding the footage is a message from Nem, which speculates that the trailer was created as an investment pitch to other publishers that "ultimately failed." What’s more, this trailer shows off what appears to be a fully-fledged campaign, with Nem saying the project shifted from a purely free-to-play online experience to a title with much more single-player content and optional online co-op.

The trailer shows Optimus Prime (seemingly not voiced by Peter Cullen, with users speculating he is instead played by Jon Bailey, who has also given voice to several Transformers characters in the past, including Optimus), saying that the Legion has invaded the galaxy and that it’s up to the Autobots to seek them out and prevent further destruction.

Footage shows Optimus, Bumblebee, and Iron Hide navigating rough terrain as they fend off the Legion, eventually teaming up with the Decepticons to purge the galaxy of this mutual enemy. It seems Megatron was a recruitable and playable character, who used a whip-like appendage, as well as a gun, to take down his foes.

Given what we’ve seen thus far, it’s even more of a travesty that this game was canceled. Transformers fans almost had something amazing on their hands, with an intriguing story, stunningly realistic visuals, and what appeared to be robust gameplay that utilized both Autobots and Decepticons.

Here it is the final trailer of transformers reactivate their latest version of the game. as you see totally different from what y'all ever seen. In it you can see: New York, Nevada desert and Cybertron. you can see bits of gameplay there and there and final designs of the cast. https://t.co/qtq0bXHIw7

— 𝓔𝓷𝓭𝓮𝓻🔛🔝 (@EnderGuyZV2) October 26, 2026

Nem is currently making a documentary about this failed project and is urging anyone with information and willing to share their story to reach out to them at a proton email linked in their bio.

Transformers: Reactive is far from the only painful cancellation to happen in the gaming space; the next Mass Effect game was also canned by EA, which shut down BioWare as part of its shift in strategy, leaving fans brokenhearted and doing everything they can to get the title out of limbo and into the hands of another developer.

items.title: Want To Smell Like a Werwulf? This Perfume Has You Covered
items.author: Rachel Weber
items.content:
Nothing says date night like the smell of "the heat of flesh that was once human." Robert Eggers' Werwulf hits movie theaters at Christmas, but you can pre-order an official perfume set based on the movie right now. Focus Features has teamed up with the very fancy Heretic Parfum for a set of three very specific fragrances.

Designed to represent each stage of a werewolf transformation, the descriptions of each of the scents are a wild ride.

  • The Wode Hath Teth: The scent of the feral woodland itself. Cold bark, frozen soil, and smoke in the air. Resinous. Mineral. Austere.
  • Werwulf: The transformation. Skin, damp earth, root, resin, and the suggestion of wet fur. Intimate. Warm. Primal.
  • Blodwode: The memory of what the forest has witnessed. Bleeding tree bark, leather, musk, and the heat of flesh that was once human. Animalic. Resinous. Untamed.

The set is limited edition, $55, and won't ship until at least November 6, but at least that's in time for Grandma's Christmas present. You can also grab each perfume individually for $125.

It's not the first movie collaboration Heretic has done. Nosferatu Eau de Macabre used notes of "wilting lilacs, velvety vegan ambergris and strikes of lightning" while one for the The Bride promised "Jasmine and rose stitched together as flesh. Cedarwood as bone. Frankincense as breath or spirit." The company is perhaps most notorious for creating the viral “This Smells Like My Vagina” candle with Gwyneth Paltrow in 2020.
